comment: What the companions say when the party rests (src/camp.cpp). Each talk is 1 to 8 lines [speaker, text]; it is only used when everyone in it is alive. Tags: any, wild (outdoors), dungeon, sla (Sla-Mori), pax (Pax Tharkas), hurt (somebody is below half their hit points). Generated by tools/camp/build_camp.py from tools/camp/*.txt.

lines: Is that rabbit I smell? Tell me that's rabbit.
It was going to be rabbit. Then it was going to be stew. Now it's mostly a rumor.
Mostly a rumor. Hrumph. You burned it, didn't you.
I only turned my back for a moment. A bird landed on my hoopak!
I'll eat the rumor. Pass the pot.
Quiet, all of you. I am trying to read.
Sorry, Raist. Can I get you some tea?
You may bring tea. You may not bring conversation.
Right. Tea. Not talking. Got it.
Someone should keep the first watch. I will take it.
You took it last night, Sturm.
A Knight does not count his watches.
A friend does. Riverwind, will you share it with him?
I sleep lightly. I will hear anything he misses.
My knees say rain by morning.
Your knees said rain yesterday, and the sky was clear as a bell.
It was a very small rain. In the next valley.
Do you ever look at the stars and wonder who is looking back?
The ancestors, my lady. So the Que-Shu taught us.
I believe you believe it. For me, that has been enough for many years.
Does anyone want to hear about the time my Uncle Trapspringer fell into a well?
He was not hurt at all. The well was hurt, I think. It had a very large dent.
A well cannot be dented, you daft kender.
Then it was a very remarkable well.
You cough, brother, when you are worried. Did you know that?
Me? You're the one who coughs, Raist.
Then you have learned it from me, and I did not teach you well.
Maybe I just learned that you cough, and I worry.
We should reach the next road by tomorrow, if the weather holds.
Then we will arrive wet and in a worse temper. I have done that before.
I could tell you stories of arriving wet.
Please do not, Flint. Not tonight.
I think I could eat a whole roast boar.
And every evening I am right. That's the dangerous thing.
I would help, but I am small and could only eat half a boar.
Raistlin, your cough sounds worse tonight. Let me look at it.
It is nothing a cleric can mend.
Then let me sit with you. Healing is not the only use of a friend.
...You may sit. You may not say anything kind.
I will try to say nothing at all.
Do you know what my father taught me about the Oath and the Measure?
I don't, but I expect you're going to tell me.
That honour is not a thing one wears. It is a thing one is, even when nobody watches.
Hrumph. Well, that's easy enough when nobody's watching.
That is precisely when it is hardest, Flint.
In my pouch. I do not remember how it got there, but it's a very nice button.
Mine now, I expect. Unless it's Sturm's.
It is not mine. Though I would like to know where it came from.
There are tracks near the camp. Old ones. A deer, perhaps two.
Nothing that walks on two legs, and nothing that wears boots.
Good. That's the kind of news I like.
The kind I like better is that they were two days old.
I keep thinking about my workshop in Solace.
The one with all the toys?
The same. Wooden birds, carved dragons, a little horse with a tail that moves.
I would like to see it again. I broke most of your toys, but I'd like to see the rest.
You did not break all of them. Some you only mended wrong.
It is strange to think we were all just travelers in an inn.
The Inn of the Last Home seems very far away tonight.
It does. And it seems small, now, compared to what we've seen.
Small and warm. I miss that part.
I miss it less. But I will miss you all when this is done.
Each of you has a skill. A sword. A bow. A kind word. I have only my mind.
That's more than all of us.
It's not flattery. You're the smartest man I ever met.
Then you have not met very many, and I pity you.
I know several, and none of them are for sharing with a kender.
I only ask because it's quiet, and a quiet camp is the sort of camp where something creeps up.
That is a fair point, Tas. Sing something very softly.
Softly? That is a very difficult thing to do.
Everyone's feet hurt. At my age, even my hair hurts.
I'm going to take my boots off.
When I was a boy I thought a Knight rode out and slew a dragon on the first day.
Now I know the dragon takes years of walking and arguing and bad weather.
It is a very unglamorous sort of heroism.
The best sort, I begin to think.
Do you think the gods are watching us?
They are watching, I do not doubt. Whether they approve is another question.
You are very certain they do not.
I am not certain of anything, except that they have not given me a reason to be warm about it.
Then let them give you one soon.
Everyone get some sleep. I'll keep an eye on the fire.
You will not keep an eye on anything. You will brood.
You brood the way other people breathe.
I'd give a fortune for a hot bath.
I would give a fortune for a hot bath and a cold pie.
I have seven fortunes. They are just not mine yet.
You are about to be, and you will snore. I am merely warning the camp.
Tell me, Tanis, did you ever think we would do something like this?
I thought I would be a half-elf with a bad beard for the rest of my days.
You are still a half-elf with a bad beard.
Yes, but now I have a reason for it.
Riverwind, how do you know where to put your feet so quietly?
By noticing where the ground says no.
Dry leaves. Loose stones. Wet clay. It tells you, if you listen.
I have never once heard the ground say anything.
I wonder what my people would think of this journey.
They would say you were chosen.
And would they say the same of you?
They would say I was fortunate to have been chosen to follow.
That is not what I asked, my love.
I know. But it is what I wish to answer.
Do you ever wish things were simpler, Raist?
What would you do, if they were?
Read, and not be interrupted. I fear that is the whole of my ambition.
I think you have a little more than that.
Do not be perceptive, brother. It does not suit you.
Nothing. That's what worries me. No crickets, no birds. Nothing.
He is right. Everyone stay close to the fire tonight.
I will keep my sword where my hand can find it.
I am going to draw a map of everything we have seen.
Mind you leave off the bit where you got lost.
I did not get lost. The places moved.
These ones did. I have the evidence.
Rarely, and never when I am watched.
I only meant that you look tired.
I look the way I look. It is the only face I was given.
Sturm, can I ask you something about being a Knight?
Do they get to eat well?
...The Measure does not address it directly.
Then I'd make a poor Knight. I've got the shoulders, but not the discipline.
Tasslehoff, what is that you are carrying?
A feather. It is a very good one. I will give it to Flint.
He says that now, but later he will make a very nice toy bird with it.
Gilthanas wears fine clothes for a man on the road.
Elves do that. They think a good coat is a courtesy.
Then I owe the road an apology.
Does anyone else feel that we are being watched?
Not especially. But I trust your instincts.
It may be nothing. A Knight learns to listen to the quiet.
The quiet is only listening back.
Tika would have a pot of stew on by now.
She would also have a sharp word for each of us.
A few, yes. But the stew would be worth it.
Hrumph. I'd trade the stew for the sharp words.
No. But I wanted to say it.
Goldmoon, tell me about the Blue Crystal Staff.
What would you like to know?
What it feels like, when it answers you.
Like a warmth in the hand, and a sense of being heard.
How very pleasant. I have never been heard that way.
What's the oldest thing any of you remember?
A very tall stump. I fell off it.
I remember a lot of things. Most of them are somebody else's.
We should go over what we know about the Dragon Army tomorrow.
I will gather what I can.
I will tell what I have seen of their camps.
Good. I fear we have only half the story.
You fear? I know we have only half. The other half does not like us.
There's a stone in my boot.
I can take it out for you.
Last time you took something out of my boot, you took the boot.
Eventually. I walked home in one shoe.
I dreamed of Solace last night.
And the little bridges, and the lamps swinging in the wind. It was so peaceful.
Then it was a good dream.
It was. I woke with tears on my face.
Think the Highlord has a cook?
Brother, you are considering the culinary skills of our enemy.
A fire is a fine thing. It makes strangers into companions.
Shall I begin? There was once a kender who found a dragon's egg in a basket of laundry...
Do you know why I travel with you?
Partly. And partly because you are going where I wish to go, and it is easier to go together.
That sounds like an honest answer.
Do not make a habit of expecting it.
Your hands shake when you hold your tea, mage.
They shake when I hold anything. I have grown used to it.
Then use both hands. It is not weakness to use both hands.
Does the moon ever get lonely, do you think?
Perhaps. But there are three of them, Tas, if you know where to look.
Three? I only ever see the white one.
The red one is called Lunitari, and the black one Nuitari, and only some of us can see the black.
How wonderful. And how rude of them.
Not just the food. The noise, you know? The everyday kind.
I know. Someday it will be loud again.
I never wanted any of this.
I only wanted a decent chair, a pipe, and my own bench to whittle at.
Hrumph. Where else would an old dwarf go, with a family like this?
Goldmoon, do you ever grow weary of leading?
I do not think of it as leading. I think of it as walking in front.
It is the same thing, from behind.
Perhaps. But I would rather be seen from behind than not trusted from the front.
It is an owl. It wants a mouse, not you.
That is a relief. I have been mistaken for a mouse before.
Raist, remember when we were small and you made a candle flame jump?
Mother was so scared she dropped the soup.
And you were not scared. You laughed.
Of course I did. It was wonderful. It still is.
I meant anyone who isn't Caramon.
I have never once been afraid to die.
I am afraid to die for nothing. That is quite different.
Then we are agreed, because so am I.
Flint, would you teach me to whittle?
It is not a lady's craft.
I am a chieftain's daughter. I may do as I please.
Hrumph. Very well. Take the little knife. Mind your thumb.
I will mind it very carefully.
I was only touching it to make sure it was not about to bite.
It is a book, kender. It has never bitten anyone.
This one looks like it might.
My people say every traveler brings a gift to the fire.
I brought nine buttons and a spoon.
I will accept the buttons. The rest is already my burden.
What did you dream of last night, Sturm?
Of a hall with a great round table, empty.
Waiting, I think. For what, I could not tell.
That is an odd one. Perhaps it is for the best.
I do not like it down here. The stone feels wrong.
Like it remembers being cut by hands that wanted it to hold a lie.
Hrumph. I'm only saying what the walls are saying.
Do you hear water dripping somewhere?
So do I. That is why I am not sleeping.
I found a tunnel that goes up!
It might lead to the surface!
It might lead to a draconian barracks. Stay by the fire, Tas.
Fine. But I want you to remember that I could have found the exit.
Strange how the darkness makes the camp feel smaller.
Yes. A friend in the dark is worth ten in the daylight.
I am glad to have you, Sturm. All of you.
The honour is entirely mine, my lady.
Walls this old hold a great deal of residue.
Magic. Or the memory of it. It lingers, like perfume in a locked room.
Everything is dangerous, if you are foolish enough. I merely observe.
Why do they build everything with so many corners?
To make it hard to get at them.
But it makes it hard to get at us too.
That is the cleverness of a corner, lad.
I feel the weight of all that stone over us.
You are safe, my love. It has stood for centuries.
It is not the falling I fear. It is the not seeing the sky.
Then think of the sky. We will see it again.
Sturm, do you think there are ghosts down here?
Only if you treat them with disrespect. The dead deserve courtesy.
I'll be extremely courteous. I'll even say good morning.
This reminds me of a dwarf hall I visited as a lad.
It was a long time ago. The gully dwarves had gotten into the cellar.
Everything. I do not wish to discuss it.
Keep your voices down. Sound travels strangely in these halls.
The stone carries it. A whisper in one chamber is a shout in another.
Likely. Which is a pity, since I dislike company.
There are marks on the wall. Scratches, in rows.
Many days. Many more than are kind.
Then let us not add to the number.
I wish there was a window.
I know. But I wish. Just a little one, with a bit of the sky.
When we leave, I'll take you to the top of the tallest tower.
Is this where the bad people keep their treasure?
This is where the bad people keep their problems. Treasure's a separate room.
Dwarven architecture. Treasure always goes behind the second door.
May I look for the second door?
I could not help but notice the carvings above the arch.
Not quite. Older. A kind of promise, I think.
To the stone, perhaps. That it would not fall.
The air is cold, but clean. There must be a way out somewhere.
Cold air moves toward the surface. We are not trapped.
That is the best thing you have said all day.
It is the only thing I have said all day.
Do you think the Dragon Army knows we are here?
Then someone is, at this moment, deciding whether to come and find us.
Thank you, Raistlin. That is not the thing I wanted to think about.
I will be happy to supply the thing you did want. It is a short list.
But the bed rolls feel like they are breathing.
I only said they felt it. I did not say they were.
I keep thinking we'll turn a corner and find the way out.
Then we will find another way, and another, until we do.
You are the only man I know who makes that sound reasonable.
It is a property of a long hall.
I keep hearing my own stomach.
That is not an echo, brother. That is you.
What do you suppose they used this room for?
Someone took what was on them. Recently, by the dust.
Recently enough that I will keep my sword near.
It is the quiet I find hardest.
Quiet is a fine thing for thinking.
Too fine. I begin to hear my own thoughts, and they are not always kind.
Then let us talk, my lady. About anything at all. Tell me of your people.
Gladly. We begin with the river.
This was a dwarf hall, once. A good one.
The arches are right. The joins are tight. Whoever laid these loved stone.
And whoever left them did not.
Aye. And I'd like to meet them, and have a word.
The mist is thicker down here.
It is not a natural mist. It carries a chill that has no season.
It is the sort of thing that is dangerous to the unprepared. Fortunately, you have me.
I do. And I'm very grateful.
Say it again, but quieter. The mist listens.
I think somebody just whispered my name.
A kind of a hiss. Like a snake saying "Tas" while swallowing.
It is only the mist and the stone.
That's what I said to myself. I did not believe me either.
There are old bones in the corner. Dwarven, from the size.
...Rest well, friend. Someone will find a bench for you yet.
Let me say a blessing. They deserve it.
Sla-Mori. A name that means little to anyone who does not know the old dwarven.
Quite. And a secret way has a way of keeping its secrets.
So do I, mage. But I do not keep them in graves.
There is a sense of something unfinished in these halls.
The dwarves who made them left in a hurry?
Or did not leave at all.
Do not say that, Sturm. I shall not sleep.
Forgive me. A Knight should know better.
I keep thinking I hear a weapon scrape.
It is the dripping, on the metal grating.
Reasonably. If it is not, we will all know soon enough.
We are very close to Pax Tharkas now, I think.
Under it, if I have the direction right.
Under a fortress. How exciting. I hope they don't know we're here.
They would be foolish not to guess.
Then I hope they are foolish.
There is a kind of sorrow in these halls.
Old sorrow, from the feel of it.
I wish I could heal it. But it is not a wound. It is a memory.
Then let us leave it a little more peaceful than we found it.
If I ever make it back to Solace, I'll tell them I slept under a dwarf hall and survived.
They don't believe me about the fish, either.
The fish was enormous. I saw it myself.
You were sitting on it, Tas.
A Qualinesti does not sleep on the ground. Our people sleep in the trees.
Then I shall make do. But please do not expect me to enjoy it.
Gilthanas, you have slept in worse places.
Last winter, in the stable. You said it was an adventure.
I never knew the stars were so many.
In the Qualinesti court, did you not see them?
Only through the windows. Here, they feel like they are sitting on my shoulders.
They are. You carry a good many of them.
I have not been fair to you. I think you have heard that before.
Then I shall say it once more, as plainly as I can. I am sorry.
Raistlin, could you show me how to light a candle with a spell?
It is not a trick, princess.
I did not say it was. I said I wished to learn how it was done.
...Very well. Pay attention. Do not pretend to be bored.
You humans waste so much time on food.
Elves live on fruit and the sun.
Laurana, why are you still awake?
I was thinking about how brave everyone is.
Being lost and walking on anyway. That is courage, I think.
You may be right. I never saw it that way.
The elf prince walks as if the ground owed him money.
I can hear you, you realize.
Good. Then you won't need it repeated.
Sturm, tell me about the Knights.
What would you like to know?
Why you believe in them, when so many do not.
Because somebody has to. And I would rather it were me.
That is the best reason I have ever heard.
I was not raised to be lonely, but the road has a way of making you so.
In your company, I am less alone. That is a rare comfort.
I do not know. I only know I am afraid of it.
Then you are in good company. The only people who are not afraid are the ones who do not understand.
Tell me, prince, what the elves say of magic.
That it is a gift, and a danger, and not to be taken lightly.
They say a great deal about mages, too. Not all of it flattering.
I should be disappointed if it were.
Tasslehoff, may I see your pouches?
They are all interesting. That is why I carry them.
Then show me the very best.
When this is over, I will return to Qualinesti.
Sit under a tree, and be quiet, and watch the leaves.
It is an ambition. I am allowed to have one.
I need a hot meal and a warm bed.
You need a better sense of proportion.
A hot meal and a warm bed is the entire proportion.
Goldmoon, how do you know you are doing the right thing?
I do not always. I act on the best I know, and I hope the gods catch what I miss.
Then I have friends who will.
Pax Tharkas. Two towers and a wall of stone. Built by men and dwarves, together.
Then it is a place of shame, and we have been sent to cleanse it.
Please do not call it a cleansing, Sturm. It is going to be a great deal of walking.
The people in the cells above. Do you think they know we are coming?
They know someone has to. They may hope it is us.
Then we must not fail them.
A dragon lives in this place.
Flamestrike. A red, and a mean one.
Of course. I have known a great many dangers, and only the fool is not afraid of a dragon.
Then I'm a fool, because I'm scared stiff.
You are many things, brother, and a fool is the least.
Free the prisoners. Find the way out. Keep the dragon from noticing.
The final item has the least chance of success.
I know. Which is why I mention it.
The Highlord is not a fool, Tanis.
No. He is something worse. He is patient.
I wish you'd stop making these things sound reasonable.
What will happen to us if they catch us?
I am trying not to. It keeps coming back, like a stray cat.
Then feed the cat a better thought.
That we will not be caught.
I saw a child's shoe near the door.
A small one, with the strap broken.
Someone's daughter walked this way, and not by choice.
Then we shall walk this way for her.
The way they turn to stone when they die, and trap your sword.
A nuisance, certainly, but a lesson in the importance of letting go.
You've never lost a sword in one.
I carry a staff. It is much easier to let go of.
Dwarves built part of this, you know. Good stonework.
It is a pity it should serve the Dragon Highlord.
Stone has no loyalty. It stays where it is put.
Nor do we, thank the gods. We are put where we choose to stand.
When we reach the top, I want everyone together.
No heroics. No wandering off to find a better fight.
He means you, Tasslehoff. And you, brother.
There are runes carved into the lintel. A ward, I think, and an old one.
Partly. It says to those who come in anger: stay out. To those who come in need: enter.
Both. I fear the ward will not know what to do with us.
There are many boot marks in the dust. Draconian, from the clawed prints.
A squad of them passed here. Not long ago.
Then we keep watch in pairs tonight.
Pairs, and no fire after midnight.
Do dragons dream, do you suppose?
Of fire, and gold, and the sound of breaking things.
It is also very large. Move along.
If we get through this, I'll build a wall around Solace.
Stone. And ale barrels, for the strategic effect.
Hrumph. Not the worst idea I've heard today.
I swore to defend the weak. There is no clearer place for that oath than here.
I know. That is the other thing I swore. To be worthy of help.
You are the most worthy man I know.
Then we are both fortunate. I am fortunate to have a friend who flatters.
Let me tend your wounds before we sleep. Both of you.
You are bleeding on my blanket.
...Fine, maybe I'm a little bit not fine.
Sit. Quietly. The gods are listening.
Three times. One of them was on the head. I didn't notice.
That explains a great deal about your decisions today.
Just fix me up, Raist. Please.
Sit still, Sturm. The cut is deeper than it looks.
It is a very large nothing. I can see the bone.
Nobody's counting the cost, but I am.
And I think we're running low on luck.
Luck is for those who need it. We have each other.
That is better than luck, if we can keep it.
Observe, brother. I am not so fragile that I cannot hold a fever for an afternoon.
The cold. It is only the cold.
...Fine. Do not mention it to anyone.
It was a respectable ruin until today.
Come, Flint. Lie down. I will help.
Hrumph. You are a kind woman. Do not let it go to your head.
I have a bandage, but it has a picture of a rabbit.
It's a very good rabbit. I drew him myself.
Then he is a hero among rabbits. Wrap the wound.
We should rest longer, I think.
We cannot afford not to. A tired Knight is a dead one.
Then we rest. Goldmoon, can you spare a prayer?
I have taken worse and walked on.
You did not walk on. You were carried.
You were carried, and you were heavy, and I am telling the story.
I wonder whether anyone has thought how often one of us has to be rescued.
Constantly, brother. It is the main activity of the party.
Then I'm glad we're good at it.
Everyone tell me how you feel.
That is all I needed to hear. We rest.
The wind is coming from the east. Dust, and something burning.
A day, perhaps. A village, or a camp.
We should find out which, and who lit it.
I see them. They do not need an announcement.
But there are so many tonight! I tried to count and lost count at two hundred and forty.
That's because you stopped to count the same one twice.
Is it true that on the plains the grass sings?
When the wind is right. It sounds like a thousand tiny flutes.
I remember it from my girlhood.
Listen now. It is nearly the same.
Why is the ground always lumpy when you want to sleep?
Because it's the ground. It never promised to be anything else.
Somebody should have a word with it.
Many have. It has not listened.
This land was once farmland, you know. Villages and orchards.
Before the Cataclysm, even. The land remembers, in its way.
The land remembers nothing. But some people remember on its behalf.
I saw a rabbit with two white feet.
I saw it too. It will make a poor supper, and a fine omen.
That is not an omen. That is a tragedy.
You hate everything but your own bench.
Well, my bench is in a tree, and trees are the right place for a bench.
Solace is a lovely place. I miss the bridges.
Everyone misses the bridges, and nobody misses the mortgage.
Do you smell that? Wild lavender.
There is some growing down by the creek.
My mother used to dry it and hang it in the lodge.
Then I will pick a handful tomorrow, and you may hang it wherever you like.
I would like to point out that we are in the middle of nowhere.
It is a considerable one, if nowhere is where something chooses to find us.
Then let's keep close to the fire.
A wise suggestion. Now observe how I took it from your mouth.
How far do you think the road goes?
To the sea, if you follow it long enough.
I have never seen the sea.
Nor I. We might go together, one day.
When we're done saving the world?
When we're done saving it, yes.
It is watching. Hawks do both.
I like hawks. They look like they know where everything is.
They do. That is why we should stay still.
Look at my sword arm. It's been aching since morning.
Then we're both right, and we're both going to get wet.
I never understood how the plainsmen could be so calm on the open grass.
There is nothing to hide behind, so there is nothing to hide.
A practical one. A beautiful thought would have a roof.
Look at the moon. Solinari is full tonight.
The white moon does not favor me. Nor does the red, when it is full.
The black favors me quite well, if anyone is asking. Nobody is.
It's a little warm. Is that normal for pebbles?
Only if you promise not to explode it.
...It is a small piece of fire-stone. Keep it dry, and keep it away from Caramon.
A fine night to sleep under the stars.
I thought you hated the open road.
I do. But I do not hate a good night's sleep, and the stars cost nothing.
That is the most cheerful thing I've ever heard you say.
Dew. It will burn off by noon.
The same way you know when someone is lying. I listen.
